title: Green Chicken Pozole with Tomatillos, Pepitas & Crunchy Toppings
dek: Tender shredded chicken and hominy simmer in a vivid roasted-tomatillo broth thickened with toasted pepitas, then finish with onion, oregano, chile and crisp tostadas.
image_alt: Earthenware bowl of pale-green chicken pozole with visible hominy and shredded chicken, topped with chopped white onion, dried oregano and red chile
ingredients: 1 1/4 lb tomatillos, husked, rinsed and quartered
2 medium poblano chiles, halved lengthwise, stemmed and seeded
1 jalapeño, halved lengthwise and seeded for moderate heat
1 large white onion, divided
6 garlic cloves, unpeeled
3/4 cup raw hulled pepitas
1 packed cup cilantro leaves and tender stems
2 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp ground coriander
2 tbsp neutral oil, divided
2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
1 1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
6 cups low-sodium chicken stock, divided
2 cans white hominy, 25 oz each, drained and rinsed
1 tsp dried Mexican oregano, plus more for serving
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus lime wedges for serving
1 tsp ground ancho chile or mild red chile powder, for serving
12 baked corn tostadas, for serving

instructions.name: Broil the green vegetables
instructions.text: Position a rack 6 inches from the broiler and heat the broiler to high. Put the tomatillos, poblanos and jalapeño cut-side down on a foil-lined rimmed sheet pan. Add half the onion, cut into four wedges, and the unpeeled garlic. Broil for 8 to 12 minutes, turning the onion once, until the tomatillos collapse and the chile skins blister deeply. Cool for 5 minutes, then peel the garlic; leave the flavorful blackened patches on the chiles.

instructions.name: Toast the pepitas
instructions.text: While the vegetables broil, toast the pepitas in a dry Dutch oven over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until they puff and begin to pop. Immediately transfer them to a plate so they stop cooking.

instructions.name: Build the green sauce
instructions.text: Combine the broiled tomatillos, chiles, onion and peeled garlic with the toasted pepitas, cilantro, cumin, coriander and 1 cup chicken stock in a tall heat-safe container. Blend until smooth but still lightly speckled, about 1 minute. Vent a countertop blender and work in batches if the vegetables are still warm.

instructions.name: Brown the chicken
instructions.text: Pat the chicken dry and season with 1 teaspoon salt. Heat the Dutch oven over medium-high, add 1 tablespoon oil and brown the thighs in two uncrowded batches for 3 minutes per side. Transfer them to a clean plate; they will not yet be cooked through.

instructions.name: Fry the sauce
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining tablespoon oil. Carefully pour in the green sauce—it may sputter—and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until slightly darker, fragrant and thick enough for a spoon to leave a brief trail across the bottom.

instructions.name: Simmer the chicken safely
instructions.text: Return the chicken and any juices to the pot. Add the remaining 5 cups stock and bring just to a boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer, partially cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, until the thickest thigh reaches 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a clean board and rest for 5 minutes.

instructions.name: Add the hominy
instructions.text: Stir the drained hominy and Mexican oregano into the green broth. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes so the hominy absorbs flavor and the broth becomes lightly creamy. If it thickens beyond a flowing soup, add hot water 1/4 cup at a time.

instructions.name: Shred and finish
instructions.text: Shred the rested chicken into bite-size pieces with two forks, discarding any firm connective tissue. Return it to the pot and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the lime juice and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, then taste and adjust with more salt or lime.

instructions.name: Dress each bowl like the photograph
instructions.text: Finely chop the remaining half onion. Ladle the pale-green broth, hominy and shredded chicken into warm earthenware or deep bowls. Top with chopped onion and pinches of dried oregano and red chile powder, matching the photographed finish. Serve lime wedges and crisp tostadas alongside rather than burying the visible soup.

why_it_works: Broiling tomatillos, poblanos, onion and garlic removes raw sharpness and adds browned depth without dulling the broth's fresh green character.
Toasted pepitas purée into the roasted vegetables, lending gentle body and nutty richness while keeping the broth dairy-free.
Cooking the chicken before adding hominy gives the meat enough time to become tender while the final uncovered simmer seasons the kernels without turning the chicken stringy.
swaps: For a milder bowl, replace the jalapeño with half a small green bell pepper; for more heat, leave the jalapeño seeds or add a second chile.
Cooked turkey can replace the chicken after a holiday meal. Make the broth without raw chicken, simmer the hominy for 20 minutes, then add 3 cups shredded cooked turkey and heat to 165°F.
If pepitas are unavailable, use 1/2 cup unsalted cashews in the sauce and omit the garnish. The broth will be slightly creamier and anyone with a tree-nut allergy should not use this substitute.
storage: Cool the pozole in shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours for up to 4 days. Store onion, pepitas, lime and tostadas separately. Reheat only the portion needed over medium heat until bubbling and 165°F throughout, thinning with stock if necessary. Freeze the ungarnished pozole for up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the refrigerator and refresh with lime after reheating.
notes: Hominy is fully cooked nixtamalized corn, not ordinary canned sweet corn; rinse it thoroughly to remove excess packing liquid.
Pepitas can jump as they toast. Use a deep pot, stir continuously once they start popping and transfer them immediately so residual heat does not scorch them.
The photographed bowl is finished simply with white onion, oregano and red chile. Crunchy tostadas and lime stay alongside so the main ingredients remain visible and the toppings stay crisp.

faqs.q: Why did my green pozole turn brown?
faqs.a: Overcooking the blended cilantro or boiling the finished broth hard can muddy its color. Blend cilantro into the roasted sauce, fry only until fragrant, then maintain a gentle simmer. The final shade should be natural pale green, not neon.

faqs.q: Can I make chicken pozole verde a day ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. The soup often tastes more integrated after an overnight chill. Cool and refrigerate it promptly, reheat to 165°F, and add fresh lime only after reheating. Keep all crunchy and raw garnishes separate.

faqs.q: How thick should pozole broth be?
faqs.a: It should be fuller-bodied than plain chicken broth but still ladle easily around the hominy. Pepitas continue absorbing liquid as the soup stands, so loosen leftovers with stock or hot water rather than serving a spoon-standing stew.

title: Adjarian Khachapuri with Feta, Mozzarella & Jammy Egg
dek: High-heat Georgian-style bread boats cradle bubbling feta and mozzarella, then finish with a just-set egg and butter to stir into the molten center.
image_alt: Boat-shaped Adjarian khachapuri with a browned bread rim, molten white cheese and a whole egg yolk on a metal peel at a hot oven
ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, 360 g, plus more for shaping
2 tsp instant yeast
1 tsp granulated sugar
1 tsp fine sea salt
3/4 cup whole milk, 180 ml, warmed to 100 to 110°F
1/3 cup warm water, 80 ml, at 100 to 110°F
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for the bowl
8 oz low-moisture whole-milk mozzarella, coarsely grated
6 oz feta, well drained and crumbled
1/2 cup whole-milk ricotta, drained if watery
2 large eggs, preferably pasteurized if serving with jammy yolks
2 tbsp unsalted butter, divided
2 tbsp chopped flat-leaf parsley, optional

instructions.name: Mix the dough
instructions.text: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the warm milk, warm water and olive oil. Stir until no dry flour remains, then knead on a lightly floured counter for 8 to 10 minutes, until smooth, elastic and only slightly tacky. Add flour 1 teaspoon at a time only if the dough sticks heavily.

instructions.name: Let the dough rise
instructions.text: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turn to coat and cover. Let rise in a warm, draft-free place for 60 to 75 minutes, until nearly doubled. A slow rise builds flavor; judge the dough by volume rather than the clock.

instructions.name: Preheat the baking surface
instructions.text: Set a heavy rimmed half-sheet pan upside down on the middle oven rack and heat the oven to 500°F for at least 30 minutes. Cut two 12-by-16-inch sheets of parchment. The inverted pan creates a flat, intensely hot surface while keeping this method accessible without a baking stone.

instructions.name: Mix the cheese filling
instructions.text: Combine the mozzarella, feta and ricotta in a medium bowl. The mixture should hold together loosely without pooling liquid. Divide it into two equal portions.

instructions.name: Shape two boats
instructions.text: Gently deflate the risen dough and divide it into two equal pieces. On separate parchment sheets, stretch each piece into an 11-by-7-inch oval. Roll both long sides inward toward the center to make thick raised rims, then pinch and twist the ends firmly into points, leaving a 3-inch-wide open channel.

instructions.name: Fill without overloading
instructions.text: Spread one portion of cheese inside each channel, stopping 1/2 inch from the rolled rim. Press the filling gently into an even layer while preserving the pointed boat shape visible in the photograph. Let the shaped breads rest for 10 minutes.

instructions.name: Bake the cheese boats
instructions.text: Slide both breads, still on their parchment, onto the preheated inverted pan. Bake for 11 to 13 minutes, rotating the parchment once, until the rims are deeply golden, the bottoms are crisp and the cheese bubbles. The bread rim should register about 200°F in its thickest section.

instructions.name: Add the eggs safely
instructions.text: Crack each egg into a small cup. Pull the pan rack out carefully, make a shallow well in each cheese center and slide in one egg. Bake for 3 to 5 minutes, until the whites are opaque and set at the edges while pasteurized yolks remain jammy. For children, pregnant people, older adults or anyone immunocompromised, continue baking until both white and yolk reach 160°F.

instructions.name: Butter, stir and share
instructions.text: Transfer each hot khachapuri to a board and add 1 tablespoon butter beside the egg. Scatter with parsley if using. At the table, stir the egg and melting butter through the cheese, tear off pieces of the browned rim and dip them into the center. Serve immediately while the filling is fluid.

why_it_works: A warm milk-and-water dough bakes into a tender interior with enough structure to contain the heavy cheese filling.
Salty feta, stretchy low-moisture mozzarella and creamy ricotta approximate the tang, pull and softness of traditional Georgian cheeses using widely available ingredients.
Baking the filled boats before adding the eggs browns the crust and melts the cheese without overcooking the yolks; the hot filling finishes the egg as it is stirred.
swaps: If you can source imeruli and sulguni cheese, use 7 ounces of each, coarsely grated, in place of the feta, mozzarella and ricotta.
For a sharper widely available blend, replace the ricotta with 2 ounces finely grated provolone and add 2 tablespoons milk to keep the filling supple.

To make four individual boats, divide the dough, cheese and butter into four portions and use four pasteurized eggs. Start checking the smaller breads after 8 minutes, then add the eggs for the final 3 to 4 minutes.
storage: Khachapuri is best immediately. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat on a preheated sheet pan in a 375°F oven for 8 to 12 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F; cover loosely with foil if the rim darkens too quickly. Do not leave a jammy egg at room temperature, and do not freeze an egg-topped bread because the texture deteriorates.
notes: The 75 minutes of rising time is included in the total but not the active prep time. A cool kitchen may require another 15 to 30 minutes.
Use low-moisture mozzarella and drain the feta and ricotta well. Wet fresh mozzarella releases enough whey to make the center soupy and the bottom pale.
Parchment brands have different temperature limits. Verify yours is rated for 500°F; otherwise shape on a well-floured peel and transfer directly to the bare preheated pan.

faqs.q: Why did my khachapuri boat open while baking?
faqs.a: The pointed ends were not sealed firmly enough or too much cheese pushed against the sides. Twist and pinch each end, keep the filling below the rolled rim and leave a small margin around it.

faqs.q: Can I prepare the dough ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Use cool rather than warm liquid, cover the mixed dough and refrigerate it for 8 to 24 hours. Let it stand at room temperature for 45 to 60 minutes before dividing and shaping.

faqs.q: Is a runny egg yolk safe in khachapuri?
faqs.a: A pasteurized egg lowers risk when you want a jammy yolk, but risk is not zero. People at higher risk of foodborne illness should use pasteurized eggs and cook both white and yolk to 160°F.

title: Silky Lemon Posset with Toasted Almonds
dek: A brief boil and fresh lemon transform cream into an exceptionally smooth, make-ahead dessert finished with crisp golden almonds—no eggs, starch or gelatin required.
image_alt: Two shallow white bowls of smooth pale-yellow lemon posset topped with toasted sliced almonds on a light wooden table
ingredients: 3 cups heavy cream, 720 ml, at least 36% milk fat
3/4 cup granulated sugar, 150 g
1/8 tsp fine sea salt
Finely grated zest of 2 large lemons, about 2 tsp
6 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 90 ml, strained
1/3 cup sliced almonds, 35 g

instructions.name: Prepare the serving bowls
instructions.text: Set six 5-ounce ramekins or shallow heat-safe bowls on a small tray that fits level in the refrigerator. Place a fine-mesh strainer over a heat-safe measuring jug or bowl with a pouring spout.

instructions.name: Warm the lemon cream
instructions.text: Combine the heavy cream, sugar, salt and lemon zest in a heavy 3-quart saucepan. Warm over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves and the cream steams. Do not walk away; cream rises quickly once it boils.

instructions.name: Boil for exactly 3 minutes
instructions.text: When bubbles cover the surface, reduce the heat enough to maintain a controlled full boil. Boil for 3 minutes, stirring and scraping the bottom continuously with a heatproof spatula. The mixture should reduce slightly without scorching or boiling over.

instructions.name: Add the lemon juice
instructions.text: Remove the saucepan from the heat and wait 1 minute for the bubbling to subside. Whisk in the strained lemon juice gradually. The cream will remain pourable but should thicken enough to lightly coat the spatula.

instructions.name: Rest and strain
instructions.text: Let the lemon cream stand undisturbed for 8 minutes so the acid can begin thickening the dairy. Pour it through the prepared fine-mesh strainer, pressing only gently on the zest, for the exceptionally smooth texture shown in the photograph.

instructions.name: Portion and chill
instructions.text: Divide the mixture evenly among the six ramekins, about 1/2 cup each. Cool uncovered for 20 minutes, then cover without touching the surface and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until softly set and no warmer than 40°F. Overnight chilling gives the cleanest texture.

instructions.name: Toast the almonds
instructions.text: Put the sliced almonds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat. Cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until pale gold and fragrant. Move them to a cool plate immediately; they darken fast from residual heat.

instructions.name: Finish like the photograph
instructions.text: Just before serving, uncover the cold possets and scatter about 1 tablespoon toasted almonds across each pale-yellow surface. Serve in the ramekins so the delicate set remains intact.

why_it_works: Boiling dissolves the sugar, evaporates a controlled amount of water and concentrates the cream so it can form a spoonable set.
Lemon acid changes the structure of the cream's milk proteins; the measured ratio thickens reliably without eggs, starch or gelatin.
Straining removes zest and any tiny cooked-milk particles, while adding almonds only at serving time preserves the contrast between silky cream and crisp garnish.
swaps: For lime posset, replace the lemon zest and juice with equal measured amounts of fresh lime zest and strained lime juice; the flavor will be sharper and more floral.
For a nut-free finish, omit the almonds and top each chilled posset with 2 tablespoons of sliced strawberries or raspberries immediately before serving.
Caster sugar can replace granulated sugar gram for gram. Do not reduce the sugar below 120 grams, because sugar affects both the flavor balance and the finished texture.
storage: Keep possets covered and refrigerated at 40°F or colder for up to 3 days. Store toasted almonds separately at room temperature in an airtight container and add them only before serving. Do not freeze the possets; thawing can make the cream grainy and cause liquid to separate.
notes: Use true heavy cream with at least 36% milk fat. Half-and-half, light cream and most plant milks do not contain enough dairy fat and protein to set by this method.
Fresh strained lemon juice provides predictable acidity and clean flavor. Bottled juice can taste harsh and its acidity varies by product.
The posset should tremble slightly and yield easily to a spoon. A rubbery or sliceable set usually means the cream boiled too long or too much juice was added.

faqs.q: Why did my lemon posset not set?
faqs.a: The usual causes are low-fat cream, too little acid or an abbreviated boil. Use 36% heavy cream, measure 90 milliliters strained juice and maintain a controlled boil for the full 3 minutes before chilling at least 4 hours.

faqs.q: Why does my posset taste grainy?
faqs.a: The cream may have scorched or the juice may have been whisked in while the boil was still violent. Use a heavy pan, stir continuously, wait 1 minute off heat before adding juice and strain before portioning.

faqs.q: Can lemon posset be made for a dinner party?
faqs.a: Yes. Make and chill it 1 to 2 days ahead, keeping each ramekin covered after cooling. Toast the almonds separately and scatter them on only when serving so they stay crisp.
